body.p: Applicant replies to the final Office Action dated December 20, 2021, in which this Reply is filed within two months. Claims 1-12 and 14-21 stand rejected. Independent claim 1 is currently amended. Support for the present amendment can be found in the originally filed specification, claims, and drawings. Reconsideration is respectfully requested. Request for Consideration in the AFCP 2.0 Program
Applicant requests for this application to be considered in the AFCP 2.0 program. Applicant submits form PTO/SB/434 with this reply. Rejections under Q 103
Claims 1-12 and 15-21 are rejected under 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent No. 4,887,016 ("Malick"), in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,315,079 (Berends). Applicant traverses the rejection.

The Patent Office takes the position that Malick discloses a first cargo handling robot 10 and a second cargo handling robot 10A. These robots 10, 10A in Malick are actually two different embodiments. The Patent Office has not identified where Malick discloses using the robots 10, 1 0A in combination to collectively move an article of any type, much less to move an article from one position on a cargo deck to a different position on the cargo deck in accordance with claim 1.

The Patent Office takes the position that Berends discloses that it is known to have robots work simultaneously to transport cargo. Berends discloses four separately displaceable lifting columns 2 which co-act to lift a bus 4. The Patent Office has not identified where Berends discloses using the four lifting columns 2 to move the bus 4 from one location on a ground surface to a different location on this same ground surface. As both Malick and Berends lack disclosure of having two different robots engage a common article to move this article from one location on a surface to a different location on this same surface, no combination of Malick and Berends can disclose the combination of features set forth in claim 1.

The Office Action asserts the presently claimed "cargo unit" is disclosed by Malick's "47 and 72" (i.e., "sensor assembly 47" and "box 72"). It is unclear which of these elements-sensor assembly 47 or box 72-is considered to be the claimed "cargo unit," or if both are considered to be the claimed "cargo unit."
With regards to the box 72, Applicant submits that Malick and Berends, alone or in combination, fail to disclose or make obvious "the first cargo handling robot and the second

cargo handling robot are configured to simultaneously couple to a common cargo unit to transport the cargo unit from a first position to a second position" as claimed. Significantly, Malick recites, "Referring again to FIG. 1, for the purpose of describing the present invention, there is illustrated for example a portion of a production line conveyor 71 by which boxes 72 are conveyed in a sequential fashion to a work station where the box remains stationary while the robot 10 operates to tighten a plurality of bolts 74 on a flange 75 at one side of the box." Thus, Malick appears to be limited to designs where Malick's robot 10 is stationary while engaging with the box 72.

With regards to the sensor assembly 47, Applicant submits that Malick and Berends, alone or in combination, fail to disclose or make obvious "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot are configured to simultaneously couple to a common cargo unit to transport the cargo unit from a first position to a second position" as claimed. Malick teaches moving the sensors to generate a reference frame for the robot to pick up a tool from the storage bracket on the back wall for performing tasks (Malick, col. 6, 1. 45 through col. 7, 1. 45). Significantly, Malick is limited to configurations where a single robot moves the sensors to create the reference frame.

Moreover, Applicant submits that "sensor assembly 47" is not within the broadest reasonable interpretation of Applicant's claimed "cargo unit." For example, the present application recites in [0021]-[0022], "Although cargo unit 20 is illustrated as a cargo container, cargo unit 20 could also be a pallet, an irregularly shaped object, an irregularly shaped container, or other cargo. Items to be shipped by air, freight, and/or the like are typically loaded first onto specially configured pallets or into specially configured containers, also known as unit load devices or 'ULDs.' In that regard, as referred to herein, cargo unit 20 may also refer to a ULD." Applicant submits that is not reasonable to construe the Malick "sensor assembly" as the "cargo unit" in the present claims. This rejection should therefore be withdrawn.
For all of the foregoing reasons, Applicant submits Malick and Berends, alone or in combination, fail to disclose or make obvious each and every feature of amended claim 1.

Independent claim 11 similarly recites, "wherein the cargo handling robot is configured to communicate with a second cargo handling robot so as to simultaneously move the cargo unit together with the second cargo handling robot." (Emphasis added). Applicant submits the above comments made with respect to claim 1 apply, mutatis mutandis, to independent claim 11.

Independent claim 17 similarly recites, "attaching the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot to the cargo unit at the first position" and "moving, via the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot, the cargo unit to the second position" (Emphasis added). Applicant submits the above comments made with respect to claim
1 apply, mutatis mutandis, to independent claim 17.

Based upon the foregoing, claims 1, 11, and 17 are allowable over Malick and Berends. All claims that depend from claim 1, 11, or 17 are thereby also allowable over Malick and Berends for the above-noted reasons. There is therefore no need to separately address the patentability of each of these claims and/or the Patent Office's interpretation in relation to any of these claims or any of the references of record in relation thereto.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are allowable and requests allowance of the pending claims. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if that would help further prosecution of the subject application. Applicant authorizes and respectfully request that any fees due or overpayments be charged or credited to Deposit Account No. 19-2814. This statement does NOT authorize payment of the issue fee.
Respectfully submitted,
